universe.detection: empirical: tickers whose series ends >30d before the dataset
universe.warning: SURVIVOR universe: zero delistings detected. Every result is an UPPER BOUND, not a measured edge (P1-7 item 1).

cost_model.slippage_applies_to: stop and market orders only (not limit fills)

no_lookahead.method: appended 40 bars of a fabricated 3x rally; every trade closing before the original data ended must be unchanged

caveats: SURVIVOR universe (0 delistings in 241 tickers) — P1-7 item 1 unfixed. Any positive result is an UPPER BOUND, not a measured edge.

known_biases: SURVIVORSHIP (largest, UNFIXED): prices.parquet is today's CORE list applied backward — spine_metadata.json records survivorship_inflation=true and today_list_applied_backward. ZERO of its 241 tickers delist, so every company that went bankrupt, was acquired, or deteriorated out of the quality screen is absent. Those are disproportionately the losers.
no PIT earnings calendar: the live engine REJECTS setups with earnings inside the holding window, the backtest cannot and so takes trades live would skip
costs are a flat bps assumption on top of adverse gap fills, not measured spread
modelled: commission + slippage as SEPARATE charges (P1-7 item 2); slippage on STOP fills only, never on limit fills, floored at max(bps, 1 tick)
order A modelled as a true STOP-LIMIT: a gap beyond the limit that never returns is NO TRADE, matching plan §6
entry gap fills at max(trigger, open) capped by the limit; stop gap fills at min(stop, open) — adverse on both sides
when one bar spans both stop and target, the STOP is assumed to hit first
the entry bar's high does not ratchet the stop (we cannot prove we held it)
